name: Timewracked Dedication — "for each mode of movement available to you"
printed: AoN feat-8166, verbatim: "Your Speed increases by 5 feet for each mode of movement available to you." It reads two ways and print settles neither: (a) +5 feet to EACH Speed the character has (land, swim, fly, climb, burrow), which is the same shape as Swashbuckler's Speed's "to your Speeds"; or (b) +5 feet to the LAND Speed, multiplied by the number of movement modes owned — so a character with land + fly walks 10 feet faster and flies no faster. No other clause in the book is worded this way, and the mythic feat's own sibling clauses give no steer.
theirs: Wanderer's Guide does not settle it either: their encoding for this record carries no Speed operation that distinguishes the two readings (one SPEED variable, so their data cannot express "each mode" at all). This is a print question, not a WG-comparison one — it surfaced only because batch 037 built the typed/plural Speed lane and had to decide, record by record, which carriers may take `speedBonusAllSpeeds`.
ours: public/core.json feats/timewracked-dedication ships `landSpeedBonus: 5`, which is NEITHER reading: it is a flat +5 to land regardless of how many movement modes the character has. Batch 037 deliberately authored no row for it — the record is off-batch (no WG packet), no finding covers it, and the engine group flagged it as residue rather than guess. The lane to carry either answer now exists: reading (a) is one row, `speedBonusAllSpeeds: true`; reading (b) needs a small formula carrier (landSpeedBonus as a string over a movement-mode count), which nothing in the engine counts today.
question: Which reading is right — (a) +5 to every Speed the character has, or (b) +5 to land per movement mode owned? If (a), the fix is one overlay row on feats/timewracked-dedication and the lane is already built. If (b), we need a way to count movement modes in a formula, which is engine work worth scoping before it is started. Either way the shipped flat +5 is wrong for some characters and right for none, so it should not stay as it is.

name: A plural Speed bonus that only applies while a STATE is on (Swashbuckler's Speed + panache)
printed: AoN feat-6238, verbatim: "You gain a +5-foot status bonus to your Speeds; this increases to a +10-foot status bonus while you have panache." Batch 037 built the first half — the bonus TYPE and the PLURAL target both reach a built character now (finding swashbucklers-speed#typed-all-speeds, 8 overlay rows plus src/rules/derive.ts). The CONDITIONAL half has no carrier: the record holds only the flat 5, and the core.json `modes` bucket has no entry for panache raising it.
theirs: Wanderer's Guide DOES encode the conditional (their live row 32855: conditional on ACTIVE_MODES INCLUDES panache, addBonusToValue SPEED 10/5, each "type":"status"), so on this one half their encoding is ahead of ours. They cannot do the plural at all — one SPEED variable — so neither side carries the whole clause.
ours: Not buildable as an overlay row, which is why no row was authored: the modes `speeds` lane SETS non-land Speeds by max and ADDS land, so it can say "+5 land while panache is on" and cannot say "+5 to EVERY Speed while panache is on". Making it say the second means the plural half (`speedBonusAllSpeeds`, built this batch in deriveSpeeds beside the speedAdjust loop) has to reach the active-mode loop too — an engine change in src/rules/modes.ts + derive.ts, with a blast radius across all 99 stances and every other mode that touches Speed.
question: Do you want the conditional half built now as its own engine lane (a mode whose Speed grant is typed and plural, which would also let every other "while you are X, +N to your Speeds" clause be encoded honestly), or parked until a batch actually reads the modes-speed lane against print? Meanwhile a swashbuckler with panache walks 5 feet short of the printed number, on land and on every other Speed. Nothing else in batch 037 waits on the answer — the type and the plural are built and green either way.

name: Flexible Spellcaster on a spellbook caster (wizard, witch, magus)
printed: AoN archetype-99: "The number of spells in your spell collection each day equals the total number of spell slots you get each day from your class spells", with "you must select at least one 1st-level spell for your collection each time you prepare" as the only stated limit. Print does not exclude book casters — a flexible wizard has BOTH a spellbook (the class feature) and a collection prepared from it, which is exactly how the archetype reads for a prepared caster.
theirs: Out of scope for the comparison: Wanderer's Guide carries no ability_block row for this record at all, so there is no encoding to compare. The finding is print-read, riding in the batch-037 read file.
ours: Batch 037 built the collection as ONE flat pool sized by total daily class slots (finding flexible-spellcaster#collection-shape, src/rules/build.ts `flexibleCollectionSize` + the across-rank rail in src/builder/Builder.tsx), on your 2026-09-10 ruling #102. It reaches only the classes that fall THROUGH to the collection branch — cleric, druid, animist. src/rules/build.ts tests `else if (sp.spellbook || cls.id === 'wizard' || cls.id === 'witch')` BEFORE `else if (archSpellMods.spellCollection)`, so a flexible wizard, witch or magus never reaches it: measured here, a 6th-level flexible wizard builds a `prepared` entry with no `slots` and no `repertoire` at all. A bare reorder is the wrong fix and also breaks test/bare-feat-lanes.test.ts "leaves the wizard curriculum slot alone", because `restrictedSlots` (the curriculum lane) is built only inside the book branch.
question: The right shape is a COMBINED branch — a book caster who takes Flexible Spellcaster keeps the spellbook and the curriculum slots AND gets the flat collection prepared from it — which is an engine-shape change to the caster branch in build.ts plus one expectation in a test file this round could not edit. Do you want that built as its own lane, or should the archetype stay unavailable to book casters until then? (It is currently neither: they can take it and silently get nothing.)
